summary: Battery-powered ESP32-S3 environmental sensor. Wakes every ~15 minutes, reads a BME280 over I2C, publishes over Wi-Fi, returns to deep sleep. No enclosure: it lives in an off-the-shelf box.

voltage_class.source: USB VBUS is the highest voltage present; the cell is a single LiPo.

application.description: Environmental monitoring for a greenhouse. Nothing depends on it.

skipped.reason: Four wires between two boards on a JST lead and an I2C pigtail. A netlist and a rendered wiring diagram would carry less information than the pin map already does, and this build has no hand-wired harness to get wrong.
No enclosure is being designed or printed, so there is no CAD handoff and no component manifest. The parts live in a bought box with a lid that already fits.
